reviews.reasoning: Independent re-derivation of Ps.78.52-55 confirms a genuine scene shift: v.52's departure verb (וַיַּסַּע, 'led out') introduces a shepherd/flock wilderness-guidance frame entirely absent from the immediately preceding plague catalogue (78.43-51), the strophe closes on settlement ('made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents,' v.55), and v.56's adversative reopens the narrative on a new footing ('yet they tempted and rebelled'). Span, warrant, and unit_type (strophe, policy-correct for this long psalm) are sound; I find no rival seam within 52-55 or at either boundary, and confidence=high is justified. One evidence-hygiene defect: the rejected_alternative's 'with no plague vocabulary carried over' and the observed_substrate_signals' 'absent from the plagues section entirely' are universal-absence claims shipped without an adjacent digit-bearing sweep (check_universals.py flags both). I independently swept ten plague-catalogue terms against the span; the underlying claim holds, but it was not swept before assertion.

reviews.reasoning: The span opens on a clear resumptive marker (וַיְנַסּוּ וַיַּמְרוּ, 'yet they tempted and rebelled,' 78.56) and closes on the denied-rites climax (78.63-64, no wedding song / no weeping) before 78.65's unmistakable divine-awakening turn — strong boundaries on both sides. I independently re-verified the two device claims at accent_stripped tier (the byte-tier variance across cited verses is cantillation-only, not a different word or form): the tempting-verb וַיְנַסּוּ recurs at exactly 78.18/78.41/78.56 (3 verses) and עֶלְיוֹן recurs at exactly 78.17/78.35/78.56 (3 verses) — both counts confirmed as claimed. The rejected_alternative's declined split at 78.59|60 is grammatically sound on inspection: 78.59-60 form one uninterrupted wayyiqtol chain (שָׁמַע...וַיִּתְעַבָּר...וַיִּמְאַס...וַיִּטֹּשׁ) with the same subject and no address or mood shift at the proposed cut. check_universals.py flags that sentence as an unswept universal, but it is a syntactic-continuity observation rather than a countable lexical claim, and I find it accurate. confidence=high, unit_type=strophe, and parent_psalm=78 are all correct; no rival seam found.

The span opens on a construction (וַיִּקַץ כְּיָשֵׁן אֲדֹנָי, 'then the Lord awakened as one out of sleep') that I independently confirm occurs at only 1 verse book-wide (both byte and skeleton tiers) and closes the psalm at its final verse (78.72), so the outer boundaries are not in question. The Ephraim-frame claim (78.9/78.67) checks out at accent_stripped tier (2 verses; the byte-tier gap between the two citations is cantillation-only, not a different word). The rejected_alternative's declined split at 78.68|69 is well-grounded and, on inspection, understated: the root בחר ('choose'/'did not choose') itself recurs at 78.67 (negated), 78.68, and 78.70, forming an election-refrain that binds the Judah/Zion and David elections into a single unit — a stronger warrant than stated for keeping v.69 (temple-building, same wayyiqtol chain, same subject, no address shift) inside the span rather than at a new boundary. check_universals.py flags 'no address or mood shift' as an unswept universal, but this is a discourse-continuity judgment, not a countable claim, and I find it accurate. confidence=high, unit_type=strophe, and parent_psalm=78 are all correct; span and warrant stand. One register defect: observed_substrate_signals labels the 78.65 construction 'a hapax within this book,' the exact flagged usage the book strategy's own installed erratum (NOTE OL-c28, §11) warns against — the staged tools can only establish book-internal (Psalms-scoped) rarity, not true hapax-legomenon status, and the erratum instructs rows to drop the term 'hapax' in favor of scoped digit phrasing ('1 verse in Psalms, tier').
